cohort: The study participants were all cases of uterine scar rupture in a post-caesarean pregnancy identified in a hospital.
finding: Multiple previous caesarean scars, lower uterine segment thickness < 2.8mm, inter delivery interval <24 months, previous emergency caesarean section, advancing maternal age, increasing BMI, and post-dated gestation were identified as factors increasing the risk of scar rupture.
mod_finding: Previous emergency caesarean section was found to increase the risk of scar rupture, and detailed history regarding previous pregnancy should be considered before a trial of vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC).
gest_age: post-dated gestation (as a risk factor for scar rupture)
